mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.impact: The processing of personal data by a data user must comply with specified data protection principles, including notice, choice, disclosure, security, retention, data integrity, and access.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user shall not—
(a) in the case of personal data other than sensitive personal data, process personal data
about a data subject unless the data subject has given his consent to the processing of the
personal data; or
mappings.impact: A data user must obtain the data subject's consent to process personal data, except in specific permitted circumstances.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.impact: The data user must provide written notice to the data subject about the processing of their personal data, including the purposes, sources, rights to access and correct data, third-party disclosures, and options to limit processing.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user shall, when processing personal data, take practical steps to protect the personal
data from any loss, misuse, modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure,
alteration or destruction by having regard—
(a) to the nature of the personal data and the harm that would result from such loss, misuse,
modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure, alteration or destruction;
(b) to the place or location where the personal data is stored;
(c) to any security measures incorporated into any equipment in which the personal data is
stored;
(d) to the measures taken for ensuring the reliability, integrity and competence of personnel
having access to the personal data; and
(e) to the measures taken for ensuring the secure transfer of the personal data.
mappings.impact: A data user must take practical steps to protect personal data from loss, misuse, modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure, alteration, or destruction, considering factors such as the nature of the data, storage location, security measures in equipment, personnel reliability, and secure transfer methods.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user forum may prepare a code of practice—
(a) on its own initiative; or
(b) upon request by the Commissioner.
mappings.impact: A data user forum may prepare a code of practice on its own initiative or upon request by the Commissioner.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
An individual is entitled to be informed by a data user whether personal data of which that
individual is the data subject is being processed by or on behalf of the data user.
mappings.impact: An individual has the right to be informed by a data user whether their personal data is being processed.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user may refuse to comply with a data access request under section 30 if—
(a) the data user is not supplied with such information as he may reasonably require—
(i) in order to satisfy himself as to the identity of the requestor; or
(ii) where the requestor claims to be a relevant person, in order to satisfy himself—
(A) as to the identity of the data subject in relation to whom the requestor claims to be the relevant
person; and
(B) that the requestor is the relevant person in relation to the data subject;
mappings.impact: A data user may refuse to comply with a data access request under certain conditions, such as insufficient identification, disproportionate burden, risk to another individual's privacy, or confidentiality obligations.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
Where—
(a) a copy of the personal data has been supplied by the data user in compliance with the data
access request under section 30 and the requestor considers that the personal data is
inaccurate, incomplete, misleading or not up-to-date; or
(b) the data subject knows that his personal data being held by the data user is inaccurate,
incomplete, misleading or not up-to-date,
the requestor or data subject, as the case may be, may make a data correction request in writing
to the data user that the data user makes the necessary correction to the personal data.
mappings.impact: The data subject or requestor may request correction of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, or outdated personal data held by a data user.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user may refuse to comply with a data correction request under section 34 if—
(a) the data user is not supplied with such information as he may reasonably require—
(i) in order to satisfy himself as to the identity of the requestor; or
(ii) where the requestor claims to be a relevant person, in order to satisfy himself—
(A) as to the identity of the data subject in relation to whom the requestor claims to be the relevant
person; and
(B) that the requestor is the relevant person in relation to the data subject;
(b) the data user is not supplied with such information as he may reasonably require to
ascertain in what way the personal data to which the data correction request relates is
inaccurate, incomplete, misleading or not up-to-date;
(c) the data user is not satisfied that the personal data to which the data correction request
relates is inaccurate, incomplete, misleading or not up-to-date;
(d) the data user is not satisfied that the correction which is the subject of the data correction
request is accurate, complete, not misleading or up-to-date; or
(e) subject to subsection (2), any other data user controls the processing of the personal data
to which the data correction request relates in such a way as to prohibit the first-mentioned
data user from complying, whether in whole or in part, with the data correction request.
mappings.impact: A data user may refuse to comply with a data correction request if they are not provided with sufficient information to verify the requester's identity or the accuracy of the data, or if another data user prohibits compliance.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data subject may by notice in writing withdraw his consent to the processing of personal
data in respect of which he is the data subject.
mappings.impact: A data subject may withdraw consent to the processing of their personal data, and the data user must cease processing upon receiving notice.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
Subject to subsection (2), a data subject may, at any time by notice in writing to a data user,
referred to as the “data subject notice”, require the data user at the end of such period as is
reasonable in the circumstances, to—
(a) cease the processing of or processing for a specified purpose or in a specified manner; or
(b) not begin the processing of or processing for a specified purpose or in a specified manner,
any personal data in respect of which he is the data subject if, based on reasons to be stated by
him—
(A) the processing of that personal data or the processing of personal data for that purpose or in
that manner is causing or is likely to cause substantial damage or substantial distress to him or to
another person; and
(B) the damage or distress is or would be unwarranted.
mappings.impact: A data subject may require a data user to cease or refrain from processing personal data if it is causing or likely to cause substantial damage or distress, with specified exceptions.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
The Commissioner may carry out an inspection of—
(a) any personal data system used by data users for the purpose of ascertaining information to
assist the Commissioner in making recommendations to the relevant data user relating to the
promotion of compliance with the provisions of this Act, in particular the Personal Data
Protection Principles, by the relevant data user; or
mappings.impact: The Commissioner may inspect personal data systems used by data users to assess compliance with the Act, including the Personal Data Protection Principles.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user shall not transfer any personal data of a data subject to a place outside Malaysia
unless to such place as specified by the Minister, upon the recommendation of the Commissioner, by
notification published in the Gazette.
mappings.impact: A data user must not transfer personal data outside Malaysia unless the destination is specified by the Minister following the Commissioner's recommendation, and the destination has laws substantially similar to the Act or ensures an adequate level of protection.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of comprehensive legal framework for data protection
mappings.verbatim_quote:
Subject to subsection (2), any person who at the date of coming into operation of this Act either
alone or jointly or in common with other persons processes any personal data or has control over or
authorizes the processing of any personal data, shall within three months from the date of coming into
operation of this Act be registered as a data user in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
mappings.impact: Any person who processes personal data as of the Act's coming into operation must register as a data user within three months.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.impact: The processing of personal data by a data user must comply with the Security Principle, which requires safeguards for personal data.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user shall, when processing personal data, take practical steps to protect the personal
data from any loss, misuse, modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure,
alteration or destruction by having regard—
(a) to the nature of the personal data and the harm that would result from such loss, misuse,
modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure, alteration or destruction;
(b) to the place or location where the personal data is stored;
(c) to any security measures incorporated into any equipment in which the personal data is
stored;
(d) to the measures taken for ensuring the reliability, integrity and competence of personnel
having access to the personal data; and
(e) to the measures taken for ensuring the secure transfer of the personal data.
mappings.impact: A data user must take practical steps to protect personal data from loss, misuse, modification, unauthorized or accidental access or disclosure, alteration, or destruction.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user shall keep and maintain a record of any application, notice, request or any other
information relating to personal data that has been or is being processed by him.
mappings.impact: A data user must keep and maintain a record of any application, notice, request, or other information relating to personal data that has been or is being processed by them.

mappings.indicator_name: Minimum period of data retention requirements
mappings.impact: Data users must comply with the Retention Principle when processing personal data.

mappings.indicator_name: Minimum period of data retention requirements
mappings.verbatim_quote:
Subject to subsection (2), a data subject may, at any time by notice in writing to a data user,
referred to as the “data subject notice”, require the data user at the end of such period as is
reasonable in the circumstances, to—
(a) cease the processing of or processing for a specified purpose or in a specified manner; or
(b) not begin the processing of or processing for a specified purpose or in a specified manner,
any personal data in respect of which he is the data subject if, based on reasons to be stated by
him—
(A) the processing of that personal data or the processing of personal data for that purpose or in
that manner is causing or is likely to cause substantial damage or substantial distress to him or to
another person; and
(B) the damage or distress is or would be unwarranted.
mappings.impact: A data user must cease processing personal data or refrain from beginning processing for a specified purpose or manner within a reasonable period after receiving a data subject notice, if the processing is causing or likely to cause substantial damage or distress.

mappings.indicator_name: Minimum period of data retention requirements
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data subject may, at any time by notice in writing to a data user, require the data user at the
end of such period as is reasonable in the circumstances to cease or not to begin processing his
personal data for purposes of direct marketing.
mappings.impact: The data subject may require the data user to cease processing personal data for direct marketing after a reasonable period, and the data user must comply with this requirement.

mappings.indicator_name: Minimum period of data retention requirements
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A data user shall keep and maintain a record of any application, notice, request or any other
information relating to personal data that has been or is being processed by him.
mappings.impact: A data user must keep and maintain a record of any application, notice, request, or other information relating to personal data that has been or is being processed.

mappings.indicator_name: Minimum period of data retention requirements
mappings.verbatim_quote:
directing the relevant data user to take such steps as are specified in the enforcement notice
to remedy the contravention or, as the case may be, the matters occasioning it within such period
as is specified in the enforcement notice; and
mappings.impact: The provision requires data users to take specified steps to remedy a contravention of the Act within a specified period, which may include data retention obligations as part of compliance.

mappings.indicator_name: Minimum period of data retention requirements
mappings.verbatim_quote:
If there is no prosecution with regard to any computer, book, account, computerized data or other document,
signboard, card, letter, pamphlet, leaflet, notice, equipment, instrument or article seized under this Act, such
computer, book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter, pamphlet, leaflet, notice,
equipment, instrument or article shall be taken and deemed to be forfeited at the expiration of a period of one
calendar month from the date of service of a notice to the last-known address of the person from whom the
computer, book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter, pamphlet, leaflet, notice,
equipment, instrument or article was seized indicating that there is no prosecution in respect of such computer,
book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter, pamphlet, leaflet, notice,
equipment, instrument or article, unless before the expiration of that period a claim thereto is made in the
manner set out in subsections (4), (5) and (6).
mappings.impact: The provision requires that seized computerized data be retained for at least one calendar month unless a claim is made, establishing a minimum data retention period.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote: (h) such access to personal data is regulated by another law.
mappings.impact: The government may access personal data without judicial authorization if it is prohibited by another law or a court order.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.impact: Government authorities may disclose personal data without judicial authorization if they reasonably believe they have legal authority to do so, or if disclosure is necessary for crime prevention or detection, or justified as being in the public interest by the Minister.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote:
(2) Subject to section 46, personal data—
(a) processed for—
(i) the prevention or detection of crime or for the purpose of investigations;
(ii) the apprehension or prosecution of offenders; or
(iii) the assessment or collection of any tax or duty or any other imposition of a similar
nature,
shall be exempted from the General Principle, Notice and Choice Principle, Disclosure
Principle and Access Principle and other related provisions of this Act;
mappings.impact: The provision allows government access to personal data without requiring a court order or judicial warrant for purposes such as crime prevention, detection, prosecution, tax collection, court-related activities, regulatory functions, and research, provided certain conditions are met.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote:
An authorized officer conducting a search under sections 113 and 114 shall be given access to
computerized data whether stored in a computer or otherwise.
mappings.impact: An authorized officer may access computerized data during a search without requiring a court order or judicial warrant.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote:
If any computer, book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter,
pamphlet, leaflet, notice, equipment, instrument or article has been seized under this Act, the
authorized officer who effected the seizure may, after referring to the Public Prosecutor, release the
computer, book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter, pamphlet,
leaflet, notice, equipment, instrument or article to the person as he determines to be lawfully entitled
to it, if the computer, book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter,
pamphlet, leaflet, notice, equipment, instrument or article is not liable to forfeiture under this Act, and
is not otherwise required for the purpose of any proceedings under this Act or for the purpose of any
prosecution under any other written law, and in such event neither the authorized officer effecting the
seizure, nor the Federal Government, Commissioner or any person acting on behalf of the Federal
Government or Commissioner shall be liable to any proceedings by any person if the seizure and the
release of the computer, book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter,
pamphlet, leaflet, notice, equipment, instrument or article had been effected in good faith.
mappings.impact: The authorized officer may release seized computerized data without judicial authorization, provided certain conditions are met.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.impact: An authorized officer may require the production of computerized data and inspect, examine, download, copy, or extract data from it without needing a court order or judicial warrant.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote:
Any computer, book, account, computerized data or other document, signboard, card, letter, pamphlet,
leaflet, notice, equipment, instrument or article seized shall be liable to forfeiture.
mappings.impact: Government authorities may forfeit seized personal data and related items without requiring a court order or judicial warrant.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A person shall not knowingly or recklessly, without the consent of the data user—
(a) collect or disclose personal data that is held by the data user; or
(b) procure the disclosure to another person of personal data that is held by the data user.
mappings.impact: The provision prohibits the collection, disclosure, or procurement of disclosure of personal data without the data user's consent, unless an exception applies.
